title: Climate-model factor separation with Shapley values and efficient sampling
summary: Climate models often feature nonlinear responses to changes in model parameters or boundary conditions. Factor separation asks how much of the resulting change should be assigned to altered factors and their interactions. Lunt et al. (2010) showed that two factor attribution methods, the \emph{linear-sum} and \emph{shared-interaction} methods, coincide for $n\le 4$ factors and conjectured this holds for arbitrary $n$. We show that the linear-sum and shared-interaction formulas are respectively the permutation and Harsanyi-dividend representations of the Shapley value. Their equality…
